text: Completing a customer service survey with Argos means you can buy a smartphone for £9.99 or £4 as a ‘thank you’.

claimReview.title: No, Argos isn’t offering bargain price smartphones for completing survey – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is false. Argos has confirmed these offers aren’t genuine.

text: Tesco’s CEO has said the company is celebrating its 100th birthday by giving away free food boxes to people who ‘like’ a Facebook post.

claimReview.title: No, Tesco is not giving away ‘free food boxes’ to celebrate its birthday – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A spokesperson for Tesco has confirmed its CEO has not said this, and the company is not giving away free food boxes. Tesco’s 100th birthday was in 2019.

text: The chickenpox vaccine is an mRNA vaccine.

claimReview.title: Chickenpox vaccine claims: fact checked – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. It’s a live attenuated vaccine which uses a weakened version of the virus to encourage immunity.

text: The UK Supreme Court has ordered a new general election.

claimReview.title: The UK Supreme Court hasn’t just ordered a general election – Full Fact

text: A photo shows an “Antifa member” who has been taped to a bin by “patriots”.

claimReview.title: Photo of person taped to bin is performance art, and nothing to do with ‘Antifa’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The image actually shows a piece of performance art in Berlin from 2015 and has nothing to do with ‘Antifa’.

text: Unemployment has risen in every single month under Labour.

claimReview.title: Unemployment has increased under Labour, but it hasn’t risen ‘every single month’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: That’s not quite right. Both the number of people who are unemployed and the unemployment rate have increased overall since Labour took office in July 2024, but both have seen some month-to-month decreases.

text: A video shows a mass funeral taking place in Sudan.

claimReview.title: Fake video of mass funeral recirculates on social media – Full Fact

text: Pope Leo XIV said: “To be called ‘woke’ in a world that sleeps through suffering is not an insult, it’s the gospel”.

claimReview.title: No evidence Pope Leo XIV said being called woke is the gospel – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: We can find no evidence that he actually said this. The earliest source we can find says it was “made up”.

text: KFC is giving away free buckets of chicken to people who like a Facebook post to honour National Chicken Wing Day.

claimReview.title: KFC is not giving away free buckets to celebrate ‘National Chicken Wing Day’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. KFC confirmed this is not a genuine offer from them.

text: An image shows a banner at a Liverpool FC match reading “Israel, you’ll never walk alone”.

claimReview.title: Image showing ‘Israel, you’ll never walk alone’ banner at Liverpool match is likely AI – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This image isn’t real and was almost certainly made using artificial intelligence.

text: Argos is practically giving away Meta Quest 3S headsets to people who fill out a form.

claimReview.title: No, Argos is not ‘practically giving away’ Meta Quest 3S headsets to those who fill in a form – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. An Argos spokesperson confirmed this is not a genuine offer from the retailer.

text: Swans in Royal Parks have been eaten by migrants.

claimReview.title: Is there evidence for Nigel Farage’s claim that migrants are catching and eating swans and carp? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There’s no evidence to support this specific claim—the Royal Parks charity says no such incidents have been reported. Reports of swans being caught and eaten elsewhere have appeared in the media over the years, though in many the identity of those responsible was not verified.

text: The Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan has announced a new proposal to build 40,000 new council homes prioritised for Muslims under the Muslim housing plan and they will be built near mosques and halal shops.

claimReview.title: London Mayor is not building 40,000 new council homes ‘prioritised for Muslims’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t true. There are 40,000 new council homes pledged to be built in London by the Mayor by the end of the decade, but these homes are not specifically for Muslims, or any particular demographic.

text: A picture shows Boris Johnson with Ghislaine Maxwell, the daughter of Robert Maxwell.

claimReview.title: Archive picture does not show Boris Johnson with Ghislaine Maxwell – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t true. The photograph is actually of Mr Johnson and his first wife, Allegra Mostyn-Owen, while they were at university together in 1986.

text: The Conservatives only built 500 prison places in 14 years, while Labour has built 2,500 in 15 months.

claimReview.title: Minister makes misleading comparison on prison capacity – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t a like-for-like comparison. The 500 figure refers to the net increase in prison capacity, taking into account new prison places as well as those taken out of commission, while the figure he gives for Labour’s record represents new places, without accounting for those no longer in use.

text: A clip shows five whales that beached in Kamchatka in Russia the day before the recent 8.8 magnitude earthquake there.

claimReview.title: Viral video does not show whales beached in Russia the day before recent earthquake – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is not a recent clip. It has been online since at least August 2023.

text: A video shows “anti-fascists” being attacked.

claimReview.title: Video of ‘anti-fascists’ being attacked is AI deepfake of Portsmouth protest – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This video isn’t real, and is a deepfake using an image from September 2024. Clues such as the text on a flag changing in the middle of the video are evidence it was made using artificial intelligence (AI).

text: The retailer Holland & Barrett is selling a box of sports supplements for £1 as part of their customer loyalty programme for people who complete a survey.

claimReview.title: Holland & Barrett isn’t selling a box of sports supplements for £1 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Holland & Barrett has confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: From October authorities will be able to review your device at any time without needing prior notice or your permission, and will be able to access your photos, private conversation and apps. This will be enforced by AI-powered scanners which will be placed in major cities in the UK.

claimReview.title: Keir Starmer hasn’t just announced mass ‘AI scanner’ surveillance of all UK phones – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t happening. The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology says the claims are incorrect.

text: 900,000 people have cancelled the BBC licence fee in a year.

claimReview.title: 900,000 people didn’t cancel BBC licence fees last year – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There was no evidence for this claim when it was first made, and according to the latest figures, the total number of TV licences (including those paid for by the BBC) actually fell by around 300,000 between March 2024 and March 2025. The data doesn’t differentiate between licences cancelled by individuals themselves or by TV licensing.

text: Under new parking rules, drivers will face a charge if their vehicle stays in the same spot for more than 48 hours, including in front of their own house.

claimReview.title: The government is not introducing a 48-hour parking limit – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not true. A spokesperson for the Department for Transport told Full Fact these claims are false.

text: President Trump said that he would go “backstage before a Miss Teen USA show” to see “girls” with no clothes on.

claimReview.title: Trump quote on being backstage at pageants didn’t reference Miss Teen USA – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: While Mr Trump did say he went backstage at pageants and saw women with no clothes on, he did not specifically mention the Miss Teen USA pageant or speak about seeing girls dressing.

text: A video shows an airport in Tel Aviv destroyed by Iran.

claimReview.title: Video does not show ‘destroyed’ Israeli airport – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This video isn’t real. It has probably been generated by artificial intelligence (AI). Tel Aviv airport hasn’t been destroyed.

text: A photo shows a girl who has gone missing in Southport or Worcester and is being sought by her family.

claimReview.title: ‘Missing’ daughter hoax posts shared on Facebook – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The photograph is of a teenager who went missing last year in the US and was found safe shortly after.

text: HAARP (the High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program) created Hurricane Melissa.

claimReview.title: No, Hurricane Melissa wasn’t caused by the HAARP research facility – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Hurricane Melissa was a natural event and could not have been created by HAARP research.

text: Small boat crossing numbers in August were lower than any August previously.

claimReview.title: How did small boat arrivals in August stack up against previous years? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The 3,567 people who arrived via small boat in August 2025 was only the lowest for that month since 2021, when 3,053 people were recorded. The 56 boats that arrived last month was the lowest number since 2019.

text: Pictures show what life looks like for “minorities in Gaza”.

claimReview.title: Photos shared with claims they show ‘life for minorities in Gaza’ were actually taken in Libya – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is misleading. These images were taken in Libya, years earlier.

text: Facebook users who fill in a customer review on a ‘hidden page’ can buy a Nintendo Switch 2 for £4 from Argos.

claimReview.title: Argos isn’t selling Nintendo Switch 2 consoles for £4 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Argos confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer was the lawyer in a 1993 court case that “laid the ground” for “illegal migrants” to be housed in hotels and receive benefits.

claimReview.title: Asylum seekers received support prior to court case involving Keir Starmer – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is misleading. Mr Starmer was involved in a 2003 court case that specifically concerned whether asylum seekers who didn't claim asylum as soon as they entered the UK would get help from the government in the form of accommodation or financial support. Most asylum seekers could already receive accommodation and financial support before this case.

text: A video shows UK police arresting an eight-year-old old boy and his friend for waving the English flag in public.

claimReview.title: Video of boys being arrested is from 2008 TV programme, and nothing to do with England flags – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t what the video shows. It is actually an edited clip from a 2008 episode of the TV programme Traffic Cops in which two children are arrested on suspicion of theft from a motor vehicle.

text: If you’ve been living with your partner for over 12 months and haven’t officially registered your relationship with the government you will now need to declare it or face a £2,000 fine.

claimReview.title: No new £2,000 fine for unmarried couples who don’t declare their status – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t true. HMRC confirmed there is no such policy.

text: Images show Egyptians throwing plastic water bottles filled with food into the sea towards Gaza.

claimReview.title: AI-generated images of people throwing bottles of food in the sea towards Gaza shared online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Some images depicting this are not real and were made using artificial intelligence. However, there are other genuine videos of people doing this.

text: From 1 October every single driver entering central London will face a £100 charge.

claimReview.title: It’s not true that all drivers now have to pay £100 to enter London – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Although some vans, HGVs and specialist vehicles that do not meet emissions standards have to pay £100 to enter the city centre as part of the Low Emission Zone, this does not apply to all drivers and isn’t new.

text: 110,000 Brits between the ages of 16 and 34 have left the country since June of this year.

claimReview.title: Figures don’t show 110,000 young Brits have left the UK since June – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This figure likely refers to the estimated net number of British nationals aged 16-34 who left the UK in the year to March 2025. We don’t know how many are estimated to have emigrated since June.

text: An image shows a girl named Meghan Roberts who has gone missing in the UK.

claimReview.title: Facebook posts searching for missing ‘first born daughter’ are hoaxes – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is a hoax. The image shared in these Facebook posts is of a girl of a different name who went missing, and was subsequently found, in the United States. Merseyside Police, Nottinghamshire Police and Lancashire Constabulary have confirmed they have no record of any such missing person.

text: The expansion of the Senedd next year will mean its 96 members and Wales’ 32 MPs give the country the highest number of politicians per head in the world.

claimReview.title: Is Wales set to have the highest number of politicians per capita in the world? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There’s no evidence this is true. There are various ways of counting the number of politicians in any given country, but Full Fact’s analysis of the data suggests even with 96 Senedd members, Wales will have fewer elected national parliamentarians per capita than several smaller countries such as San Marino, Iceland and Montenegro.

text: A new law will restrict people from playing music in moving vehicles, resulting in a £120 fine and three penalty points on your licence.

claimReview.title: No, a new law isn’t being introduced to stop people playing music while driving – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. No such new law is being introduced, although there are already rules about avoiding distractions while driving, including playing loud music.

text: From January 2026, under the new Road Access Act in the UK, operating a vehicle without a valid licence will no longer lead to criminal proceedings, but instead will result in a civil fine similar to a parking ticket.

claimReview.title: The government is not changing the penalty for driving without a licence – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: A spokesperson from the Department for Transport confirmed that it will remain a criminal offence, although the penalty for driving without a licence may include a fine. The Road Access Act does not exist.

text: Like every Labour government in history, the previous Labour government left unemployment higher than they found it.

claimReview.title: Kemi Badenoch’s claims about Labour’s unemployment record aren’t quite right—here’s why – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is true of most Labour governments, including the two covered by current data. But historic data shows unemployment did fall during the Labour minority government of 1924.

text: Resident doctors are asking for an almost 30% pay rise on top of the 5.4% rise awarded this year.

claimReview.title: Telegraph overstates resident doctors’ pay demands – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Incorrect. The BMA has asked for a rise of 29% on top of last year’s pay, not this year’s. Its figures suggest this would equate to a rise of 22-23% on top of the increase announced this year.

text: A video shows people leaving Tel Aviv “in droves”.

claimReview.title: Footage of a Russian pilgrimage shared with claims it shows Tel Aviv ‘exodus’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Incorrect. The footage actually shows a Russian Orthodox pilgrimage filmed in Russia in early June 2025, before the latest Iran-Israel conflict began.

text: From October, bus pass rules are being modernised and people will have to re-verify their bus passes, and provide updated proof of age, residency and disability. There will also be rush hour limits in some council areas, restricting travel at peak times.

claimReview.title: People will not need to ‘re-verify’ their bus passes from October – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The Department for Transport has confirmed these claims are incorrect.

text: John Lewis is offering Bugaboo Butterfly strollers for £2 or £3.

claimReview.title: John Lewis Bugaboo offer is not real – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. John Lewis has confirmed that no such offer exists.

text: A photo shows a large Union Jack hanging from Rochester Castle as part of the recent movement to raise flags in public spaces across the UK.

claimReview.title: Viral photo of Rochester Castle with Union Jack predates recent movement to raise flags in public – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is misleading. The photo predates this movement, and shows the flag raised to celebrate the 80th anniversary of VE Day in May 2025.

text: Photos show Banksy’s most recent mural, which depicts a judge hitting a person on the ground who is holding either a St George’s or Union Jack flag.

claimReview.title: Photos of Banksy mural edited to feature England flags – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. These photos have been edited. The original photos of the mural show someone holding a placard, not a flag.

text: From January 2026 every purchase above £20 will need digital ID verification.

claimReview.title: No, you won’t need digital ID for cash payments over £20 in the new year – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. There is no evidence such a policy is coming into force. Videos purporting to be of the Prime Minister making this announcement feature fake audio.

text: A video shows an Iranian drone in Israel.

claimReview.title: Old video of Kyiv drone attack shared as recent footage of Israel-Iran conflict – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This video dates back to October 2022 and shows a drone attack in Kyiv, Ukraine.

text: A skilled migrant will contribute on average £16,000 a year towards our economy, whereas a British skilled worker contributes £800 a year.

claimReview.title: Was Sadiq Khan’s claim about migrant and UK-born workers’ contributions to the economy accurate? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t what Migration Advisory Committee data shows. A study found that in 2022/23 a migrant skilled worker made an average net fiscal contribution of £16,300, higher than the £14,400 of a UK-born working adult. But the £800 figure refers to the net contribution of an average UK-born person (including non-workers), not a “British skilled worker”.

text: The Pfizer Covid-19 vaccines contain “cancer-causing SV40”, a virus which was used in experiments to cause mice to develop tumours.

claimReview.title: Covid-19 vaccines do not contain ‘cancer-causing’ SV40 monkey virus – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not correct. The vaccine does not contain the SV40 virus, which has been used to induce cancer in laboratory animals. It uses a fragment of the SV40 DNA sequence, which does not cause cancer or produce an infectious virus.

text: Scottish travel vlogger Emma Witters was killed in the West Bank.

claimReview.title: False claims Scottish travel vlogger was killed in West Bank spread online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t true. It’s been confirmed that Ms Witters died in Hawick, Scotland.

text: A pictured couple is on the run in the UK after being charged with the death of an eight-month-old baby.

claimReview.title: Posts claiming a couple is ‘on the run’ after the death of an 8-month-old baby are hoaxes – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Both Greater Manchester Police and Surrey Police told us they were not investigating this. Gloucestershire Constabulary has not put out an appeal for the suspects, and the mugshots included in the Facebook posts were shared by police in the US in 2021.

text: A video shows an Indian pilot landing by parachute after being shot down by Pakistan.

claimReview.title: Video shows Pakistani paraglider, not ‘shot down’ Indian pilot – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This video shows a recreational Pakistani paraglider several weeks before the recent India-Pakistan crisis began.

text: A new “sustainable wardrobe order” will be introduced in January, meaning people who exceed their monthly limit on fast fashion purchases will be fined £65.

claimReview.title: Fast fashion purchases will not be limited from January – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. No such policy is being introduced.

text: Keir Starmer says the government is cutting the state pension in April 2026 to 80% of its current value.

claimReview.title: The PM hasn’t said state pension will be reduced in April 2026 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The government’s commitment to the ‘triple lock’ guarantees that the state pension increases annually, and we’ve seen no evidence to suggest that it is going down next year.

text: Last year 695,000 Brits left the UK.

claimReview.title: Around 250,000 Brits emigrated last year, not 695,000 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This figure is an estimate of the total number of people who emigrated in the year ending June 2025, 252,000 of whom were British nationals.

text: King Charles has bypassed Parliament to freeze the powers of London’s mayor Sadiq Khan, by invoking a power called the “sovereign safeguard authority”, which has effectively halted the mayor’s control over the capital.

claimReview.title: No, King Charles has not used ancient royal power to limit mayor’s control of London – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is false. There is no such thing as the “sovereign safeguard authority” and the British monarch does not have the power to take control of a city from a democratically elected politician.

text: An image shows migrants stealing a swan to eat from Winsford Marina in Cheshire.

claimReview.title: Police have said there’s ‘no evidence’ images show migrants stealing a swan to eat – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Police say there’s no evidence for this. In a statement issued when the image first circulated the local force said the men in question appeared to have been trying to take a picture with the swan.

text: From 12 September, shoppers won’t be allowed to enter any supermarket without a government-issued photo ID.

claimReview.title: Supermarkets won’t require people to show ID to enter – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t true. The British Retail Consortium, a trade association which counts most of the UK’s largest supermarkets as members, says it is “completely false” and there are no such plans.

text: Heathrow and Gatwick airports are introducing a new £50 entry fee.

claimReview.title: Heathrow and Gatwick aren’t introducing £50 airport entry fees – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. We’ve found no evidence of any such fee being announced, and Gatwick Airport said it wasn’t aware of any such charge being introduced.

text: Anyone who holds savings above £500 in a bank will be placed onto a national monitoring register, with their details shared with HMRC, the DWP and the Home Office, under a new government scheme beginning on 1 October.

claimReview.title: No, people who have more than £500 in the bank will not be placed on a national monitoring register – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t happening. HMRC told Full Fact that the claim is “completely false”.

text: We’ve already brought the number of asylum hotels down from 400 at the peak of the previous government to 200 now.

claimReview.title: How many asylum hotels have been closed under Labour? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Almost all of this decrease took place before Labour came into government. In its first year in office Labour reduced the number of hotels used to house asylum seekers by a net of three, from 213 in July 2024 to 210 in July 2025.

text: A picture shows a family who have claimed asylum in the UK and been given a new five-bedroom house.

claimReview.title: Edited picture shows Afghan family in Canada, not UK – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: The family in the picture are from Afghanistan. The original image shows them settled in Canada, not the UK. A different background has been added to the viral image.

text: A video is being shared with implied claims it shows a dog being cooked outside in Dublin by “third world” immigrants.

claimReview.title: Video doesn’t show dog being cooked by immigrants in Dublin – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t true. The footage actually shows a pig being roasted at a community event.

text: A picture shows police taking down a Union Jack from a lamp post.

claimReview.title: Photo does not show police ‘taking down a Union Jack flag’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Cumbria Police says the photo actually shows officers fitting a camera at a local church after vandalism reports, and confirmed the flag “stayed put”. We have seen no other evidence to contradict this.

text: Aldi is giving away “free food boxes” to anyone who engages with certain social media posts.

claimReview.title: Aldi is not giving away ‘free food boxes’ in return for Facebook likes – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is not a genuine offer from the retailer.

text: The government has detained and removed over 35,000 people with no right to be here.

claimReview.title: Have 35,000 people been ‘detained and removed’ from the UK under Labour? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is misleading. While there were around 35,000 immigration returns during Labour’s first year in government, most were not detained or forcibly removed. Government data shows that only around a quarter of these departures were “enforced” returns.

text: The man who tackled one of the suspected gunmen in a recent shooting at Bondi Beach is called Edward Crabtree.

claimReview.title: Man who tackled Bondi Beach suspect misidentified online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is false. The man filmed tackling one of the alleged attackers has been publicly named by officials as Ahmed al Ahmed.

text: The police estimated that three million people attended the “Unite the Kingdom” event in London.

claimReview.title: Did police estimate three million people attended the ‘Unite the Kingdom’ march? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The Metropolitan Police estimated that between 110,000 and 150,000 people attended.

text: Primark is giving away free hampers to celebrate its birthday to anyone who ‘likes’ and comments on certain Facebook posts.

claimReview.title: Primark isn’t giving away hampers to people to celebrate its birthday – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is not a genuine offer from the company.

text: The Spending Review means total departmental budgets will grow by 2.3% a year in real terms.

claimReview.title: Spending Review 2025: fact checked – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This headline figure doesn’t tell the whole story. 2.3% is the average annual real terms growth between 2023/24 and 2028/29, and includes both day-to-day and capital spending. The average annual increase between the current financial year and 2028/29 is 1.5%.

text: Gallbladder stones can be flushed out of your body, often with a diet of apples and olive oil.

claimReview.title: Do ‘gallbladder flushes’ actually remove gallstones from the body? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not a proven treatment. The stones “flushed” out of a person’s body are unlikely to be gallstones, and research has demonstrated that they’re probably created by the “flush” diet itself.

text: One in five children are obese when they finish primary school.

claimReview.title: Official child obesity figures include tens of thousands of children who aren’t clinically obese – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This figure is based on a broader definition of obesity than the one that doctors use to assess individual patients, and includes tens of thousands of children who aren’t clinically obese. Around 15% percent of children in Year 6 are clinically obese, which is more like one in seven.

text: Under the Conservatives living standards were at an all-time low.

claimReview.title: Did living standards reach an 'all-time low' under the Conservatives? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: We can’t find any data to support that and the Resolution Foundation says the PM “clearly misspoke”. At least one measure suggests growth in living standards over the last parliament was the weakest on record, and other measures of living standards saw decreases, but none of these actually reached an all-time low.

text: The government has announced that anyone over the age of 60 will be charged £5 to see their GP.

claimReview.title: Over-60s won’t be charged £5 for a GP appointment – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The government has made no such announcement, and the videos claiming this are fake.

text: Donald Trump said he’ll buy England and make it the 52nd state.

claimReview.title: Donald Trump isn’t ‘buying England’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There’s no evidence Mr Trump said this.

text: Amazon is offering iPhones to people over 50 for £2.95.

claimReview.title: Another fake Amazon offer appears on Facebook – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Amazon has confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: In 233 days as foreign secretary, David Lammy racked up £521,525 in food and drink expenses, working out at £2,238 a day.

claimReview.title: Facebook posts falsely claim David Lammy personally spent half a million pounds on food and drink expenses as foreign secretary – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is misleading. This figure appears to refer to the entirety of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office procurement card spends of over £500 in restaurants and bars, covering a four month period. It is not David Lammy’s personal food and drink expenses.

text: A clip of a large fire in a built-up area shows an Iranian attack on Tel Aviv.

claimReview.title: Video of motorcycle fire in China shared as Iranian attack on Tel Aviv – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. It actually shows a fire at a motorcycle parking lot in China.

text: A video shows a man striking several women at a train station in London.

claimReview.title: Footage of man striking women at ‘London’ station is actually from Barcelona last year – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: The incident actually occurred at Barcelona’s Camp de l'Arpa metro station in 2024.

text: The government will enforce healthy shopping habits by fining people whose loyalty cards or digital receipts show they buy too much unhealthy food.

claimReview.title: The government is not going to track people’s shopping and fine them for buying unhealthy food – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The government has announced no such policy.

text: Donald Trump once told People magazine that Republicans were “the dumbest group of voters in the country”.

claimReview.title: Fake Donald Trump quote circulates online yet again – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. People magazine says it has no record of Mr Trump saying anything like this.

text: The TV licence fee will double for everyone over 65.

claimReview.title: The TV licence fee is not doubling for over 65s – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A BBC spokesperson confirmed this isn’t true.

text: A photo shows missiles in the sky above Tel Aviv last week amid strikes between Israel and Iran.

claimReview.title: ‘Tel Aviv’ missiles image almost certainly AI, contrary to online claims – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This image was almost certainly created with artificial intelligence. There’s no evidence to suggest it’s real.

text: A live NASA broadcast from the International Space Station accidentally showed a studio technician, proving this space footage is fake.

claimReview.title: International Space Station video has been altered to make it look like a fake – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not true. The ISS footage is genuine, but has been digitally altered by adding a man drinking and waving to make it look staged.

text: The High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP) of the University of Alaska Fairbanks is behind the recent earthquake in Myanmar.

claimReview.title: No evidence Myanmar earthquake caused by HAARP research facility – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There is absolutely no evidence to support this claim and experts say the earthquake was a natural disaster. There’s no evidence HAARP is able to affect the weather or cause earthquakes.

text: From 2 January 2026, millions of workers will see a brand new £90 deduction called the “Debt Recovery Contribution” appear automatically on their monthly payslips.

claimReview.title: The government won’t be taking £90 from people’s payslips to tackle the national debt – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. There are no plans for any such policy.

text: Tesco is giving away a free box of food to people who like a Facebook post, with the additional chance of winning £100 cash.

claimReview.title: Tesco is not giving away free food boxes to people who like a Facebook post – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A spokesperson for Tesco confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: Argos is giving away laptops to the over-50s for £9.95.

claimReview.title: Fake Argos laptop giveaway posts shared again online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Argos has confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: A video compilation shows fireworks being set off in Tehran in Iran to celebrate “the greatest victory”, following the announcement of a ceasefire with Israel.

claimReview.title: Firework video clips do not show ceasefire celebrations in Tehran – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Most of the clips in the compilation actually show scenes from Nagaoka Firework Festival in Japan. We could not see any reports of major fireworks displays celebrating the ceasefire in Iran.

text: Argos is giving away iPad Pros for £2.50 to people who fill in a survey.

claimReview.title: Argos is not ‘giving away’ iPad Pros for just £2.50 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Argos has confirmed this is not a genuine offer from them.

text: Toby Carvery is giving away a free carvery for two to people who like and comment on a Facebook post.

claimReview.title: Toby Carvery CEO isn’t giving away free meals to people who comment on Facebook posts – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is not a genuine offer from Toby Carvery.

text: An image shows Barack Obama alongside “Michael before he transitioned.”

claimReview.title: Image of the Obamas has been edited to promote false claims about Michelle’s gender – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is an edited image of Barack and Michelle Obama in which the latter’s face and hair has been altered. It’s an example of longstanding baseless claims about Mrs Obama’s gender.

text: 2.4 million households in Britain have cancelled their BBC TV licence fee since 2020.

claimReview.title: How many households have cancelled the BBC TV licence fee since 2020? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: We’ve found no evidence to support this figure, which the BBC says it doesn’t recognise. There are no published figures specifically on cancellations. According to the latest data the number of TV licences in force dropped by 1.49 million between 2020/21 and 2024/25.

text: Naz Shah MP said: “Those abused girls in Rotherham and elsewhere just need to shut their mouths. For the good of diversity.”

claimReview.title: Quote wrongly attributed to Labour MP still circulating online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Ms Shah didn’t say this. She retweeted then deleted this quote from a parody account on Twitter (now X) in 2017, which she has said was a “genuine accident”.

text: The Daily Mail has published an article about a street artist painting a mural depicting Benjamin Netanyahu as Hitler after being commissioned by a “Zionist group” to celebrate Israel’s offensive in Gaza.

claimReview.title: Fake Daily Mail article about Netanyahu mural resembling Hitler shared online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not a real article published by the Daily Mail. It was created by an Australian street artist as satire and there’s no evidence these events occurred.

text: From 18 September, if you withdraw more than £200 in cash a week your bank must send your transaction details to the UK’s Financial Intelligence Unit.

claimReview.title: Cash withdrawals over £200 will not be automatically reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A spokesperson for the National Crime Agency, which oversees the Financial Intelligence Unit, confirmed this isn’t true.

text: A photo shows Donald Trump embracing convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

claimReview.title: Edited photo of Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein circulating again – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This image has been altered. The original shows Mr Trump in 1995 with his daughter Ivanka, but her face has been edited out and replaced with Epstein’s.

text: A list of the UN’s “Agenda 2030 Mission Goals” includes plans for one world police force, the end of all private property and world depopulation.

claimReview.title: Fake UN ‘Agenda 2030’ list circulates again on social media – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The UN has confirmed the list is not  genuine.

text: A photo shows a young Keir Starmer decorating a Christmas tree with Jimmy Savile.

claimReview.title: Thousands share faked photo of Keir Starmer and Jimmy Savile decorating a Christmas tree – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This photo has been edited to include Savile’s face. The original image shows the PM with an older woman, reportedly his grandmother.

text: A female police officer named Thelma Jakes has gone missing in various UK locations.

claimReview.title: Facebook posts falsely claim a female police officer is missing – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Police forces for various areas across the UK have confirmed they don’t have an officer named Thelma Jakes, meaning the alert is not genuine.

text: Anyone looking to work or live in the UK will need to have digital ID.

claimReview.title: Digital ID won’t be mandatory for everyone living in UK – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t correct. The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology confirmed a digital ID will only be mandatory if people wish to work and therefore not everyone living in the UK will need to hold one.

text: A photo shows a missing child who was found in Lowestoft in Suffolk and is being looked after by local police.

claimReview.title: Missing child hoax post shares photo of boy who died in US – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This photo shows a child who died in the US. Suffolk Police confirmed they don’t know of any such missing person case.

text: The chickenpox vaccine is pointless when you can get immunity through exposure.

claimReview.title: Chickenpox vaccine claims: fact checked – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: It’s true that immunity is gained through exposure, but the vaccination campaign in the US has been associated with a 97% reduction in chickenpox cases. This helps protect people from rare complications and those who are vulnerable.

text: Biopsies spread cancer and aren’t necessary to diagnose it.

claimReview.title: Yes, biopsies are necessary for diagnosing cancer – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Biopsies are necessary to diagnose and plan treatment for cancer. The spreading of cancer cells known as ‘seeding’, is a rare complication of the procedure.

text: A clip of a commotion amongst a small crowd of people in a corridor shows recent disorder inside an Israeli bunker.

claimReview.title: Footage does not show scenes inside ‘Israeli bunkers’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The video was filmed at Tbilisi City Court in Georgia on 12 June, and is unconnected to the recent Israel-Iran conflict.

text: A video shows a child being kidnapped by two migrants in Dublin.

claimReview.title: Police say no offence committed in relation to ‘Dublin kidnapping’ clip – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The police in Ireland confirmed no criminal offence occurred in relation to the clip.

text: A video shows a woman claiming that her baby is transgender and was born a boy but now uses “she/her” pronouns.

claimReview.title: Video of woman claiming her baby is transgender is satirical ‘rage bait’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This video is satirical ‘rage bait’, intended to provoke and generate engagement, and is several months old at least.

text: The UK has the largest ‘female health gap’ in the G20 and the 12th largest globally.

claimReview.title: Does the UK really have the 12th largest ‘female health gap’ in the world? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This claim is based on very unreliable research from a male wellness company, which was deleted after Full Fact queried it. We can find no generally accepted definition of the ‘gender health gap’, but women in the UK have a longer life expectancy and healthy life expectancy than men, although they do experience a number of health disadvantages.

text: The government is introducing a “travel quota system” that will limit British citizens to two flights per year from 15 November 2025.

claimReview.title: No, the government isn’t limiting Brits to two flights a year – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. There is no credible evidence of such a policy being introduced and videos purporting to be of the Prime Minister making this announcement feature fake audio.

text: People aged over 50 can get a Cadbury ‘Dairy Milk Family Treat Box’ or ‘Ultimate Chocolate Basket’ for £10 if they fill in an online form.

claimReview.title: ‘Cadbury’s offer’ for over 50s on Facebook isn’t genuine – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is not a genuine offer from  Cadbury.

text: A video shows 500,000 people marching in London for a recent Great British National Strike demonstration.

claimReview.title: Video does not show ‘Great British National Strike’ protest in London – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: The footage is of a different protest organised by Tommy Robinson in July 2024. The Metropolitan Police says a Great British National Strike protest in London on 24 May was attended by no more than a couple of hundred people.

text: The Department for Work and Pensions is increasing the Christmas Bonus this year from £10 to £200.

claimReview.title: The Christmas Bonus paid to some on benefits isn’t rising from £10 to £200 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The Christmas Bonus will remain £10 in 2025. However, the DWP is offering larger amounts of money as part of other schemes to some people who get certain benefits.

text: John Lewis is giving away Staub cast iron pots for £10 to over-50s who fill out an online form.

claimReview.title: John Lewis isn’t giving away expensive cast iron pots for £10 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: John Lewis has confirmed this offer is not genuine.

text: The government has announced a wealth stability tax for homeowners over 60.

claimReview.title: The government hasn’t announced a ‘wealth stability tax’ for homeowners over 60 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The Treasury confirmed there is no such tax.

text: The Premier League is banning rainbow laces and rainbow captain’s armbands.

claimReview.title: Has the Premier League ‘banned’ rainbow armbands and shoelaces? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. While the Premier League has ended its participation in the ‘Rainbow Laces’ campaign, it has confirmed it hasn’t “banned” players from wearing rainbow laces or armbands.

text: A BBC article shows Martin Lewis being arrested and describes how he has endorsed “an AI-powered trading platform” called Swiftgate Montark.

claimReview.title: Fake ‘BBC’ article falsely claims that Martin Lewis has been arrested – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: The page in question is not a BBC article, and Martin Lewis has not been arrested or endorsed such a program.

text: Fortnum & Mason is selling ‘Family Hampers’ for £10 to people aged over 40 who fill in a short questionnaire.

claimReview.title: Fortnum & Mason isn’t selling ‘Family Hampers’ for £10 to the over-40s – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The company has confirmed this isn’t a genuine offer.

text: Amazon is “giving away” laptops to the over-40s for £5.

claimReview.title: Amazon is not ‘giving away’ laptops to the over-40s – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Amazon has confirmed this is not a legitimate offer from them.

text: A screenshot shows a protester visible in the background of a recent meeting between Keir Starmer and Donald Trump holding a sign saying “Trump is a c***”.

claimReview.title: Protester did not hold up sweary sign in background of Starmer and Trump meeting – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This scene has been altered. The picture of the protester is from Donald Trump’s 2016 visit to Scotland, and has been edited into the background.

text: Carp have been taken from ponds and eaten by migrants.

claimReview.title: Is there evidence for Nigel Farage’s claim that migrants are catching and eating swans and carp? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There have been some anecdotal reports in the past of migrants, particularly eastern Europeans, poaching carp, though we’ve not found any verified recent reports.

text: The Labour government is to raise the state pension age to 74.

claimReview.title: No, the government has not raised the pension age to 74 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. The government has not announced any plans for the state pension age to be increased to 74. The state pension age is currently set to increase to 68 by 2046, but this was legislated for more than a decade ago.

text: Keir Starmer has announced a 32-hour working week in the UK starting in 2026.

claimReview.title: Keir Starmer has not announced a 32-hour working week from 2026 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. No such policy has been announced. The social media videos claiming this feature inauthentic audio with old footage of Mr Starmer.

text: A photo shows several women and girls wearing pink in Epping.

claimReview.title: Picture of ‘pink ladies of Epping’ isn’t real – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This image is not real. It was generated with AI.

text: Donald Trump said he would go “backstage before a Miss Teen USA show” and see “girls” with no clothes on.

claimReview.title: Edited Trump quote shared with misleading claims about teen beauty pageants – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: While Mr Trump said in a 2005 interview that he would go backstage at some beauty pageants and see women with no clothes on, he did not mention Miss Teen USA or talk about seeing teenage girls getting dressed.

text: Vaccines cause autism.

claimReview.title: Vaccines have not caused a rise in autism in Vietnam – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Vaccines are proven not to cause autism.

text: Boots is selling “SOL Ultimate-Body” gift sets for £3 to people who are over 25 and who fill in a survey.

claimReview.title: Boots is not selling Sol de Janeiro gift sets for £3 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This is not a genuine offer from Boots.

text: The owner of two missing dogs is seeking help to be reunited with their pets.

claimReview.title: Series of posts supposedly looking for missing pets are hoaxes – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: These posts are hoaxes. The dogs were found in Wolverhampton and have been in the care of an animal charity since March.

text: A video shows Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer saying those involved in putting up Union Jacks or St George’s flags will feel the full force of the law and will be dealt with within a week.

claimReview.title: Video of PM talking about Southport rioters shared out of context – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This clip is from August 2024 and shows Mr Starmer talking about those involved in the Southport riots. It is not related to the recent movement to raise St George’s or Union Jack flags across the country.

text: A video shows Vladimir Putin criticising the UK’s plans to bring more Gazan children to the UK for treatment, saying it “is not generosity, it’s PR”.

claimReview.title: Video of Vladimir Putin criticising UK’s ‘hypocrisy’ on Gaza isn’t real – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: We’ve found no evidence Mr Putin said this, and the creator of the video has said it is a “fictional dramatisation”.

text: A compilation video shows clips of flooding in Texas on 13 July.

claimReview.title: Viral video compilation of Texas floods is AI – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: These clips aren’t real and were made using AI.

text: From 1 January 2026 every purchase over £1,000 will be automatically reported to HMRC to crack down on money laundering, benefit fraud and undeclared income.

claimReview.title: Purchases over £1,000 will not be automatically reported to HMRC from 2026 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. HMRC has confirmed this isn’t true.

text: There are more teachers than when the Conservatives left office.

claimReview.title: How has the number of teachers changed under Labour? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t supported by the latest figures which show a fall, not a rise, though the timeframe of the data doesn’t necessarily give us a good picture of the change under Labour. There were around 400 fewer FTE teachers in England overall in November 2024 than in November 2023, but we don’t know how the number of teachers has changed in the year since.

text: New footage shows recent Israeli attacks in Iran.

claimReview.title: Video compilation includes faked clips of Israeli missile strikes on Iranian bases – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Three of these clips are not real, and were probably made with artificial intelligence. One clip appears to be genuine footage of the strikes in June this year.

text: Amazon is offering last year’s laptops to retirees in the UK for just £3 during the period 1-3 July. The retailer is also giving away all laptops from 2022-2024 to UK pensioners ‘aged 50 and over’ for just £5.

claimReview.title: Fake Amazon laptop offers circulate ahead of Prime Day – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Amazon has confirmed these are not legitimate offers from the company.

text: The government’s decision to “cancel” local elections went as high as the Supreme Court and they upheld the lower court decision.

claimReview.title: Angela Rayner didn’t ‘break the law’ by postponing some local elections – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: We could not find any evidence of legal challenges being brought against the government over the postponing of the local elections, in the Supreme Court or anywhere else.

text: Everyone who likes a Facebook post gets a free food box from Aldi as part of the supermarket’s birthday celebrations.

claimReview.title: Aldi is not giving away free food boxes in exchange for Facebook likes – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A spokesperson for the retailer confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: A 73-year-old woman with “chronic memory loss” called Naomi Adams has gone missing in various locations in the UK.

claimReview.title: Hundreds share hoax Facebook appeal for missing mum with ‘chronic memory loss’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is a hoax. The image shared in these Facebook posts is of a woman with a different name who went missing, and was subsequently found, in the United States.

text: Under Labour, the UK’s national debt is set to rise every single year until it is the size of the entire economy.

claimReview.title: Is the UK’s national debt set to match the size of the economy? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: It’s true that public sector net debt is forecast to increase every year until 2029/30 in nominal and real terms, though as a percentage of GDP it is set to peak at 96.3% in 2028/29, then fall slightly.

text: A video shows what appears to be an MP at the despatch box in the House of Commons asking why, if the US can conduct an operation in Venezuela to capture Nicolás Maduro and put him on trial, it is “impossible to capture Benjamin Netanyahu from Israel and bring him before [an] international court”.

claimReview.title: Video appearing to show MP’s question in Commons about capture of Maduro is AI – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is a fake AI-generated video. There is no serving MP that matches the likeness of the man seen speaking in the clip, and the original video features OpenAI’s Sora watermark, indicating that it was generated using artificial intelligence.

text: Russia's defence spending is at 43% of its GDP.

claimReview.title: Russia’s defence spending is not 43% of its GDP – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There’s no evidence to support this figure. Precise estimates vary, but think tanks have suggested that Russia’s defence spending was 6.7% or 7.1% of its GDP in 2024. Similar forecasts for this year put it at between 6.1% and 7.5% of the country’s GDP.

text: All UK citizens will be required to have digital ID.

claimReview.title: Will ‘all UK citizens’ have to have digital ID? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Incorrect. Under the government’s plans digital ID will be required in order to work in the UK, but the government says people who aren’t looking to work (for example, pensioners) won’t have to have one.

text: A new rule will mean that passengers at major UK airports like Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester will have to pay a £10 fee to use the toilet.

claimReview.title: No, UK airports aren’t introducing £10 toilet fees – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Both Heathrow and Gatwick airports have confirmed there are no such plans to start charging people for using toilets.

text: The UK’s electricity is the most expensive in the world.

claimReview.title: Does the UK have the ‘most expensive’ electricity in the world? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This could do with some context. Official government figures show the UK has the highest industrial electricity prices compared to International Energy Agency and EU member states, but not necessarily the highest domestic prices. Additionally, this data only looks at a range of other developed economies.

text: A picture shows European leaders and politicians sitting on chairs in a White House corridor waiting to speak to the US president Donald Trump.

claimReview.title: Image of European leaders waiting in White House corridor isn’t real – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This picture isn’t genuine—there are a number of clues that it was created using artificial intelligence (AI).

text: Resident doctors in England have had a 21% real-terms pay cut since 2008/9.

claimReview.title: Have resident doctors really had a 21% real-terms pay cut? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This figure relies on a number of questionable assumptions. In particular, it’s calculated using an unreliable measure of inflation. Other measures suggest the drop has been less—our independently verified analysis using a measure backed by the Royal Statistical Society puts it at more like 6-7%.

text: Cadbury is offering Facebook users a Dairy Milk family treat box for £10 in return for filling out a short form.

claimReview.title: Cadbury is not offering Facebook users £10 ‘treat boxes’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Cadbury has confirmed this offer is not from them.

text: From 1 October every pet dog and cat in the UK will be subject to a £100 annual fee.

claimReview.title: No, the government is not introducing a £100 annual pet fee from October – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not a real government policy. A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs told us it is completely false.

text: A video shows the Duchess of Sussex being arrested.

claimReview.title: Video claiming to show Meghan being arrested is AI – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This isn’t a real video, and this incident didn’t happen. It has been created with artificial intelligence (AI).

text: The government has deported 30,000 people in the last year.

claimReview.title: Not all immigration removals count as ‘deportations’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Not quite. The government says 30,000 people have been returned, but this includes both enforced removals and voluntary returns, and so not all of them match the official definition of a “deportation”.

text: A video shows a British soldier confronting a police officer about arresting people for ‘words’ and saying they are a ‘disgrace to their uniform’.

claimReview.title: Video of soldier shouting at police officer is AI-generated – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t real. This clip has been created with artificial intelligence.

text: The government is introducing a £27 or £25 monthly WiFi charge for all households to fund digital infrastructure.

claimReview.title: A £27 monthly ‘WiFi charge’ is not being introduced in the UK – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t happening. The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology has told us this is completely false.

text: From 1 November, the government is ordering mandatory livestock reductions as part of a climate compliance plan to cut emissions.

claimReview.title: No, the government hasn’t ordered ‘mandatory livestock reductions’ this month to cut emissions – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This isn’t a real policy announced by the government, and AI has likely been used to imitate Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer’s voice.

text: B&Q is offering cheap or free garden soil for people who complete a survey.

claimReview.title: A fake offer for cheap garden soil from B&Q is circulating on Facebook – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. B&Q confirmed this is not a real offer.

text: A video shows a Chinese cargo plane carrying aid for Gaza escorted by smaller aircraft for protection, entering Gaza through Egypt.

claimReview.title: Video shows military exercise over pyramids not China delivering aid to Gaza – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t accurate. The video actually shows a joint military exercise between Egypt and China above the pyramids.

text: The Covid vaccine is unsafe.

claimReview.title: Covid vaccine claims at the Reform UK conference: fact checked – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is not correct, according to regulators and other experts. The Covid vaccines approved for use in the UK have met strict standards for safety and effectiveness.

text:
An image shows a man who resembles
Arsen Ostrovsky, a man who was injured in the Bondi Beach mass shooting, smiling as a woman applies fake blood to his face.

claimReview.title: Fake AI image of Bondi Beach victim having blood applied circulates online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This image is fake. It has an invisible watermark which flags it as having been made or edited with Google AI. There are also a number of discrepancies and visual glitches that are hallmarks of being created with artificial intelligence. Arsen Ostrovsky did suffer a head wound in the attack in Sydney.

text: Lidl is giving away free food boxes worth £40 to people who like and comment on a Facebook post.

claimReview.title: Lidl is not giving away free food boxes to people who like a Facebook post – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A spokesperson for the retailer confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: An 18-year-old babysitter and her boyfriend are on the run in March 2025 after murdering a 1 year old in Prestbury, Cheshire.

claimReview.title: Hoax post claims couple is on the run in Prestbury after killing a child – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Cheshire Constabulary has said no one is being sought as no such incident has occurred.

text: A video shows Iranian strikes on Ben Gurion airport in Tel Aviv.

claimReview.title: Video does not show Iran attack on Ben Gurion airport – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: It actually appears to show the northern Israeli city of Haifa, which was hit by strikes on 15 June.

text: A news article from 1927 shows America was sold to five billionaires; the Rothschilds, Rockefellers, DuPonts, Harrimans and Warburgs.

claimReview.title: Claim America was sold to ‘five billionaires’ in 1927 is satire – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This article isn’t real. It was published by satirical outlet The Onion in 2005 and has been shared out of context.

text: Nine-in-10 nurses in England, Wales and Northern Ireland voted to reject the 3.6% pay award for 2025/26.

claimReview.title: Did ‘nine out of 10 nurses’ reject their pay award? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This needs context. 91% of nurses who took part in a vote said the pay award was not enough—but only 56% of Royal College of Nursing members who were consulted actually voted.

text: A video shows flash floods hitting Brenham in Texas.

claimReview.title: Viral video compilation does not show floods in Texas – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t correct. None of the six clips featured show flooding in the US city of Brenham.

text: New analysis has estimated that migrants’ partners cost Britain £5.6 billion over their lifetime.

claimReview.title: The Times corrects inaccurate headline about cost of ‘migrants’ partners’ – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Incorrect. This figure is actually an estimate of the total net lifetime fiscal cost of people who arrived in the UK in 2022/23 through the Partner route of the Family visa—which includes the partners of some UK-born British citizens.

text: Morrisons is giving people over 40 food boxes for £10 if they fill out an online questionnaire.

claimReview.title: Morrisons isn’t giving people over 40 food boxes for £10 – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Morrisons has confirmed this is not a real offer from them.

text: A video shows recent anti-immigration enforcement protests in Los Angeles, United States.

claimReview.title: Old video shared with claims it shows recent US anti-immigration enforcement protests – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Incorrect. This video dates back to May 2020 and shows protests in the city sparked by the killing of George Floyd.

text: Donald Trump said that “trans people don’t exist”.

claimReview.title: Clip of Donald Trump saying ‘trans people don’t exist’ isn’t real – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This video isn’t real and is probably AI-generated. The original footage shows the US president made no such comments.

text: Argos is selling Apple Watch 9s for £3 to people who fill in a survey.

claimReview.title: Argos isn’t selling Apple Watch 9s for £3 to people who fill in a survey – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. A spokesperson for Argos confirmed this isn’t a genuine offer from the retailer.

text: Videos show King Charles reporting that a leaked ‘royal insult’ from Prime Minister Keir Starmer is leading to political instability.

claimReview.title: Videos of King Charles discussing Starmer ‘insult’ are fake – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. There is no evidence King Charles said this and we could not find any reports of a ‘leaked’ royal insult from the Prime Minister. The audio is fake and almost certainly AI-generated.

text: If you take out more than £420 in a single cash withdrawal in the UK, your bank will be required to report it to the government’s anti-fraud division from September.

claimReview.title: No evidence banks will have to report cash withdrawals over £420 to anti-fraud unit – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: UK Finance, the trade body for banking and financial services, told Full Fact this wasn’t something that it is aware of and we couldn’t find any evidence of such a policy.

text: A video shows Iran attacking a US airbase in Qatar with ballistic missiles.

claimReview.title: AI-generated video shared with claims it shows Iran attack on US airbase in Qatar – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. This video isn’t real and features OpenAI’s Sora watermark, indicating that it was generated using artificial intelligence.

text: Unemployment has risen every single month since Labour came into office.

claimReview.title: Kemi Badenoch’s claims about Labour’s unemployment record aren’t quite right—here’s why – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: Both the number of people who are unemployed and the rate of unemployment have risen overall since last July, but not in every single month.

text: Keir Starmer has announced that from 1 November the government will reduce internet speeds from midnight until 6am.

claimReview.title: The government isn’t going to slow the internet at night from November – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. No such policy has been announced. Social media videos claiming this feature fake audio, which was almost certainly AI-generated, over old footage of Mr Starmer.

text: Migrants crossing the Channel are 24 times more likely to go to jail than British citizens.

claimReview.title: Are ‘Channel migrants’ 24 times more likely to go to prison than British citizens? – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This figure is not reliable, based on the details reported. The Conservatives’ analysis reportedly compares 2025 prison data to 2021 population statistics which are likely out of date, and appears to use data on the imprisonment of foreign nationals in general to draw conclusions about small boat arrivals specifically.

text: Screwfix is offering a “Gorilla garden cart” for £3 to over-50s.

claimReview.title: No, Screwfix is not offering huge discounts to the over-50s – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Screwfix has confirmed this is not a genuine offer.

text: Donald Trump called Elon Musk “mediocre”, said he is “constantly high on ketamine” and suggested he “go back to Africa” in a post on Truth Social.

claimReview.title: No evidence Donald Trump called Elon Musk ‘mediocre’ on Truth Social – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: There is no evidence this is a genuine post from the president and the White House says it is fake.

text: An image appears to show the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad.

claimReview.title: AI-generated image of Air India crash shared online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This isn’t a real photograph of the crash, and experts say it has been generated with artificial intelligence (AI).

text: A compilation video shows clips of a tsunami striking Russia in July 2025.

claimReview.title: Footage showing tsunami engulfing Russian towns is AI-generated – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: At least four of the 10 clips in this compilation have been previously identified as AI-generated and were shared prior to the recent tsunami. The other clips were also likely made using AI.

text: A video shows the Mikeno boat in the Global Sumud Flotilla arriving on the shores of Gaza.

claimReview.title: Video does not show Global Sumud Flotilla boat arriving in Gaza – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: The footage actually shows crowds on Sidi Bou Said beach in Tunisia in September 2025 showing support for the Global Sumud Flotilla. The Mikeno boat was intercepted by the Israeli military and did not land in Gaza.

text: Social media posts show a two-year-old boy who has been found and taken to a police station in East London, Wellingborough (Northamptonshire), and Northfield (Birmingham).

claimReview.title: Image of ‘found’ two-year-old actually shows child injured in dog attack more than a decade ago – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is a hoax. Such an incident has not been recognised or recorded recently by the Metropolitan Police, West Midlands Police or Northamptonshire Police. The image in the posts dates back to 2014 and shows a boy injured in a dog attack in the United States.

text: People can no longer take cash out of the bank and have to give HMRC advance notice if they are withdrawing cash of £3,000 or more, as well as providing evidence of how it will be spent.

claimReview.title: No requirement to notify your own cash withdrawals to HMRC, contrary to online claims – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: HMRC confirmed there is no such requirement to notify cash withdrawals to them. It’s true that banks may require some advance notice for large cash withdrawals, as well as identification and more information about the withdrawal.

text: A picture shows Donald Trump in his 50s dancing with a 13-year-old girl on Jeffrey Epstein’s private island.

claimReview.title: Picture of Donald Trump with teenage girl isn’t real – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This image isn’t real. It has the hallmarks of having been created by artificial intelligence.

text: A video shows Donald Trump speaking about the India-Pakistan conflict, in which he claims that India has violated the ceasefire with a drone attack on Pakistani civilians.

claimReview.title: Video of Donald Trump talking about India and Pakistan is a deepfake – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This video has been fabricated. It is an old clip of the US President from 2020, which has been altered using artificial intelligence (AI) to create a deepfake.

text: London Mayor Sadiq Khan, under the Muslim housing plan, is building 40,000 new homes for Muslims only, to be near mosques and halal shops.

claimReview.title: False claim London Mayor is building 40,000 new homes ‘for Muslims only’ circulates online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: This is inaccurate. The Mayor of London has pledged to build 40,000 new council homes by the end of the decade, but these are not earmarked for a specific demographic.

text: Photos and videos show the arrest of an “attempted mass shooter” near Stamford Bridge stadium in west London.

claimReview.title: Incorrect claims about arrest of ‘attempted mass shooter’ near Stamford Bridge stadium circulate online – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: These pictures and videos actually show a 16-year-old boy being arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm.

text: Tesco is giving a free meal deal away to people who like a Facebook post and follow a link.

claimReview.title: Posts claiming to offer a ‘free Tesco meal deal’ aren’t genuine – Full Fact
claimReview.textualRating: False. Tesco has confirmed this offer is not genuine.
